pr_title: RFC: drivers: modem: gsm_ppp: Optimizations and implement on/off
pr_body:
`gsm_ppp_start` and `gsm_ppp_stop` were introduced in #28475 that allows the modem to be turned on and off in the software level. After the merge of #34548, it is now possible to control the on and off of the modem in hardware level for the `gsm_ppp` modem.

This PR aims to:
1. cleanup some unused code,
2. changed how the driver is being compiled based on the Kconfig,
3. use a FSM for the setup, instead of the previous enum + boolean combo
4. further implement the `gsm_ppp_start` and `gsm_ppp_stop` so that it now turn off the hardware when the modem isn't in use to achieve power saving for battery operated devices.

fixes #33998
pr_comments: May I have your comments please @mniestroj @jukkar @rlubos @nandojve
@endian-benjamin Do you have time to review this?
I'll have a look.

Summary: 

- I really like the FSM for setup but it could be utilized better if you changed gsm_ppp_start/stop return error on illegal state transitions
- I think capturing all different modem power on/off sequences in this way would be tricky so personally I think the value of integrating power ops here is not that great. If gsm_ppp is supposed to be in charge of modem power, I would prefer generic implementations of `modem_power_on()` and off, but `__weak` linked so that the default behavior can be easily overridden by the app, without forcing the app developer to patch Zephyr.

@endian-benjamin Thanks for the review and comments!

1. Personally I don't have a usecase for the return value (yet), but I agree that the function can be more helpful to return error code instead of erring silently.
2. Do you mean separating the hw on/off out from the current `gsm_ppp_start/stop` into something like `gsm_ppp_power_on/off`? This sounds reasonably as well.

___

I think the having `__weak` sounds to be a good idea, but I'm not sure how it can be overridden outside of the `gsm_ppp`, especially when the `modem_context.h` is a private header and the `gsm_modem` is a private struct

Taking Quectel modem as an example, the reference manual states that to power off properly, user has to send AT command or press the power key and wait for the modem to reply "OK" before cutting off the power, that would at least require the `gsm_modem` struct to be public.

I do plan to expose that struct (some time later) so that it is possible to implement vendor-specific functions for the `gsm_ppp` in a separate header file which allows the `gsm_ppp` to be kept as generic as possible.

Well as you say yourself, Quectel requires weird solutions and many others do as well. And many custom PCBs will require weird solutions even if they run a "standard" modem, because some hw designer decided to skip some pins or whatever. 

Furthermore, power-on sequences called in the gsm_ppp setup loop has some implicit requirements - sleeping will cause the sys workq to get blocked, etc. All in all, the downsides to having gsm_ppp handle power-on becomes pretty apparent.

Personally, I'm not sure I see the huge upsides. What we do is usually something like `CONFIG_GSM_PPP_AUTOSTART=n`, then do the power-on sequence independently in the app or some other board-specific driver and THEN call `gsm_ppp_start()`. To restart the network stack, we just do

```
gsm_ppp_stop();
board_specific_modem_power_off();
board_specific_modem_power_on();
gsm_ppp_start();
```

Sure, this adds some boilerplate compared to letting gsm_ppp handle it under the hood, but I'm not convinced removing this boilerplate would be worth the downsides.

I'm open to discussion on it though - let's ping people. Perhaps this is even crucial enough to discuss at a developer meeting?

Moving to `gsm_ppp` from the `bg9x` modem driver that I initially used, I always have the impression that the `gsm_ppp` is missing the dts key bindings that the `bg9x` has, so all this while from my perspective the `gsm_ppp` driver is missing the on/off functions. Note tho that even if I am not convinced regarding gsm_ppp handling power ctrl, I still think the setup FSM is a clear improvement. I would welcome that patch set for sure.

I still think that it makes sense to do power control inside the driver so that it is more self-contained in the sense that the driver itself has the ability to fully control the hardware such as performing a power cycle if necessary (i.e. hardware not responding, max retries reached)

Having the turn on sequence in the `gsm_configure` makes it possible to retry the sequence if the hardware took too long to be AT ready.

I read a bit of how current modem being turned on in Zephyr:
1. hl7800 requires at least "pwr_on" and "reset" pin to asserted or deasserted
2. ublox sara has a "power pin" that needs to be held for a duration, reset seems to be optional
3. bg9x has a "power pin" that needs to be held for a duration
    - Same goes for other Quectel modems like EC2X/EG9X
    - My experience based on Quectel's evaluation board is that the reset pin itself is enough to turn on a modem, though power key/AT cmd is required to turn it off properly. From my experience, turning off the power works just as fine.
4. wnc_m14a2a requires quite a few more pins than power and reset

So seems like having a power key and reset pins are enough to turn on/off most of the modems supported in Zephyr, and most, if not all of Quectel modems. Power src pin for modem with power key is kind of a bonus to make sure that the modem is completely cutoff, it might be useful for modems that automatically boots up when powered and doesn't require a power key, however I'm not aware of any.

My opinion would be to:
- Expose `modem_context.h` so that it can be included in application
- Implement `__weak` linked `gsm_mdm_on_ops` function that does whatever necessary for the modem to be AT ready.
  - Only power source, power key and maybe reset implementation are supported in `gsm_ppp`,
- Implement `__weak` linked `gsm_mdm_off_ops` function that does whatever necessary to turn off the modem completely.
  - Power source and power key are supported in `gsm_ppp`
  - If AT cmd is required to turn off a modem then we will have to expose `modem_cmd_handler.h` and have the `sem_response` as an argument so that it is possible to override this in application.

issue_context.title: modem: gsm_ppp: Adding power key sequence for Quectel and possibly other modems
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Some modems like Quectel has a power key pin that requires a special sequence to power on or off the modem. The current `gsm_ppp` doesn't take care of that. With this change the `gsm_ppp` driver could increase its coverage to at least the Quectel EC2X series.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'm suggesting that this power on sequence to be added to `gsm_ppp_start` & power off sequence to be added to `gsm_ppp_stop` such that the on or off of the driver can be controlled by the driver itself instead of application.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Creating another driver based on the current `gsm_ppp` but for device that requires power on/off sequence is also possible, but I'm not sure if this is the right way going forward as that might end up having different PPP drivers with only minimal differences.

**Additional context**
I tested ARM's mbed-os for a short while before I decided to move on to Zephyr. I'm using Quectel EC21 and in mbed-os the EC21 is basically plug and play, the [EC2X driver](https://github.com/ARMmbed/mbed-os/blob/master/connectivity/drivers/cellular/QUECTEL/EC2X/QUECTEL_EC2X.cpp) only contains some AT commands and power on/off sequence.

review_comments: Why this change? We typically tend to include `IS_ENABLED` checks within C code instead of preprocessor when possible - it gives better code coverage during compilation. Same would go for some other places below.

Well now that you have a machinery for tracking state completely, changing the prototype of start/stop to return `int` would make sense imo. There's currently a problem where stopping gsm_ppp is hazarduous if the configuration loop is currently running - making start/stop return error codes would be a huge mitigation.
I don't think removing the ifdef wrap makes much sense, unless you explicitly verified that gcc is smart enough to realize `state == CONTROL_CHANNEL` is never true.

I don't really understand, are you referring to the removal of `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_GSM_MUX)` in L832?
I removed it because `mux_setup` is only called if `CONFIG_GSM_MUX` is true so there isn't a need to check that again.

Required for `gsm_ppp_start` to run

```c
gsm->state = GSM_PPP_STOP;
```

I'm not in favor of changes within this commit - as mentioned earlier, it's easier to introduce some regression if preprocessor checks are used and some particular configuration is not covered by the CI. IMO it's against what we typically do in Zephyr.
@rlubos meaning if I do `#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_GSM_MUX)` the mux related functions will not be checked in CI?

It really depends on what samples are actually enabling gsm_ppp module and this particular feature (you'd need to analyze paritcualr samples and their sample.yaml files to see what's actually being built).

> It really depends on what samples are actually enabling gsm_ppp module and this particular feature (you'd need to analyze paritcualr samples and their sample.yaml files to see what's actually being built).

That means if we modify the `tests/drivers/build_all/modem`'s testcase.yaml it is possible to test these different features?
Build, not test. From what I see, that particular test project seems only to build some certain configurations, it does not have any test cases defined.
It's the bare minimum I'd say.
But then we are compiling hundreds of lines of basically dead codes for users who aren't using the uart_mux and unused modem-specific's mux enabling steps in `mux_enable`

Yes, you're right, we're wasting some micro/milliseconds for the extra compilation. But we benefit from better compiler code coverage, and this approach is preferred in Zephyr:
https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/reference/util/index.html#c.IS_ENABLED
